summary: Wilhelm von Humboldt worked in linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied under Joachim Heinrich Campe, Johann Jakob Engel, Christian Konrad Wilhelm von Dohm, Ernst Ferdinand Klein, Georg Christoph Lichtenberg, Christian Gottlob Heyne, and Antoine-Léonard de Chézy at Viadrina, Göttingen, and Jena. He founded the University of Berlin, serving there around 1809–1810, and served as Prussian Minister around 1819.
Will B. Miller is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under Janet Gyatso and also studied under Lopen Chorten in 2012.

Will Sweetman works in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Lancaster University (around 1993–1996) and the University of Cambridge (around 1996–2000), and held a post at the University of Otago around 2005.

Will Tuladhar-Douglas specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Oxford (including Wolfson College, attested 2002), lectured in the history and anthropology of religion at the University of Aberdeen, and served as Director of the Scottish Centre for Himalayan Research.

Willard Gurdon Oxtoby worked in religious studies and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Stanford, Princeton, and Harvard. He taught at McGill (1960–1964) and Yale (1966–1971), held a professorship at Trinity College, Toronto (1971–1999), and was founding director at the University of Toronto (around 1976–1980).
Willard J. Peterson is a sinologist and historian who studied under mentor Denis Twitchett. He served as a professor at Princeton University (attested 1981).

Willard Van Orman Quine worked in philosophy and linguistics. He studied at Oberlin College and Harvard University, where he also served as Junior Fellow (1933–1936) and Assistant Professor (1940–1978). Later appointments included Oxford (around 1953–1954) and Wesleyan University (1964–1965).

Willem Bollée was an Indologist who studied at Utrecht University and completed his habilitation at the University of Hamburg. He served as assistant professor at the University of Münster (1971–1978) and as lecturer and professor at the University of Heidelberg (around 1968–1993).

Willem Caland worked in Indology and linguistics. He completed his doctorate at Leiden University under Carel Gabriel Cobet and Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern. He later taught Indology and held the Chair of Sanskrit at Utrecht University (1902; 1906–1929), alongside a post at Leiden (1913–1914).

Willem van der Molen specializes in linguistics, history and archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (around 1970–1983) and held posts at Leiden University (around 1984–2017) and the University of Indonesia.
William Blackstone studied at Charterhouse School and Pembroke College (around 1738–1744). He later held a post at the University of Oxford around 1753–1766.

William C. Chittick works in religious studies, philosophy, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tehran (around 1966–1974) and held posts at Sharif University of Technology, SUNY Albany, and Stony Brook University.

William C. Kirby is a historian and sinologist who studied at Dartmouth and Harvard, including under Philip A. Kuhn. He held professorial and administrative posts at Washington University in St. Louis (around 1980–1992) and served as Dean at Harvard University (around 1992).

William Carey was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Golok Nath Sharma and Ramram Basu. He was appointed Professor of Sanskrit at Fort William College in 1801 and founded Serampore College and the Baptist Missionary Society.

William Dwight Whitney worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Williams College, Yale under Edward Elbridge Salisbury, Berlin under Albrecht Weber, and Tübingen under Rudolf von Roth. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Yale University from 1853 to 1894.

William Edelglass is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies. He has held teaching posts at Colby College (attested 2007), Marlboro College (attested 2013), and the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics.

William Edward Soothill was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at University College London. He served as President of Shanxi University in 1911 and as Professor of Chinese at the University of Oxford from 1920.

William Erskine was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He was educated at the Royal High School, Edinburgh, and studied at the University of Edinburgh from around 1787 to 1792.
William Evans Hoyle was educated in the United Kingdom, studying at the University of Manchester from around 1871 to 1874 and at Christ Church from around 1874 to 1877.
William Frederic Sinclair worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He was educated at the Royal School, Armagh, and entered the Indian Civil Service in 1866.
